author: architecture-closer
role: The retention/custody disposition that closes threat-model V10. v4 decided WHAT must be proved and WHO owns proof adequacy. evidence.v1 selected the proof construction. This artifact decides the remaining third: what happens to a sealed authoritative Run when its evidence stops being available, and how that changes typed outcomes without rewriting history.
purpose: Resolve V10 by selecting (1) the per-Run custody policy, (2) the availability model for retained evidence, and (3) the mapping from evidence loss to typed host outcomes — using only the already-closed D9 vocabulary.

v10RequiredResolution: Select and independently verify an evaluation proof that covers exact activation, every outcome, relational findings, no-match and verdict derivation
Select the retained verification/regeneration closure and a per-Run custody policy before durable authoritative Runs are enabled
State how purge changes current evidence availability without rewriting the sealed Run

item1.detail: E1 requires a non-empty required universe plus exact activation by member-set identity (unique evaluationId+predicateId with recomputed universeCommitment match; count equality explicitly insufficient). E9 forbids ignoring indeterminate/error outcomes. The no-match construction is a sorted-leaf Merkle subject-set commitment plus predicateId plus coverageId. verdictDerivation is itself an evaluation carrying its own proof. E10 binds subjectScopeCommitment, the field C-2 declared and left unspecified.
item1.executable: artifacts/check-evidence.py — 13 counterexamples each rejected BY THEIR NAMED INVARIANT; --selftest rejects 15 mutations
item1.note: This item was resolved by the EVIDENCE surface and never written back to TM. Recording it here is bookkeeping, not new design.

item2Closure.detail: E2 requires the fact partition pinned by content-addressed ref OR a complete regeneration closure of non-empty locally resolvable objects; a bare digest or true boolean is insufficient. E8 requires an offline-executable derivation closure for replayable.

sealedVersusEffective.rule: A Run seals exactly one assurance capability and one evidence inventory. Both are immutable in the Run's semantic identity. Current availability lives in a separate append-only retention ledger at evidence-unit granularity. A reader DERIVES an effective capability from the sealed capability and live unit states. The effective capability is never stored in the sealed Run and can never exceed it.
sealedVersusEffective.why: The sealed capability is a historical fact about what was promised and proved at seal time; it cannot become false later. What changes is whether the retained material can still establish it. Making that a derived read-time value satisfies RA-5/E5 without either rewriting history or pretending nothing was lost.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: read-time indeterminate for every read of a degraded Run
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Forces every consumer, including plain inspection, to handle indeterminate. Making 'show me last quarter's Run' hard-fail because the Run is merely old destroys the historical record's usefulness without protecting anything: inspection asserts no authority.

Needs no new machinery, but directly contradicts v4 immutabilityAndRetention.reporting ('one Run-wide degradation word is insufficient') and would escalate a targeted privacy purge into destroying whole unrelated Runs. Would require amending v4 rather than completing it.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: availability projection with no outcome change
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Lets a Run whose proof is gone still present as a clean authoritative pass. That is RA-CE-2 (a no-match accepted after its subject material is gone) reached by a different route, and it is the exact failure the architecture exists to reject.

capabilityLattice.note: Labels are inherited unchanged from retention-tiers.v4 and evidence.v1 and remain deliberately unbound to the v3 C0/C1/C2 identities (A1-RTV4-04).
capabilityLattice.authorityFloor: An authoritative gate, baseline mutation, waiver decision, or compliance assertion requires effective capability >= verifiable. 'recorded' is advisory only — that authority text is already normative in both v4 and evidence.v1; this artifact makes it operative at read time.

capabilityDerivation.unitRequirement: Every retained evidence unit declares requiredForCapability: the LOWEST lattice level that needs it. A unit is needed for level L iff rank(unit.requiredForCapability) <= rank(L).
capabilityDerivation.supportable: Level L is supportable iff every unit needed for L is AVAILABLE.
capabilityDerivation.downwardClosure: Supportability is downward closed: a lower level requires a subset of the units, so if L is supportable every level below L is supportable. The maximum is therefore well defined.
capabilityDerivation.function: effectiveCapability = max { L : rank(L) <= rank(sealedCapability) AND L is supportable }
capabilityDerivation.floor: recorded is supportable whenever the Run manifest itself resolves. If the manifest does not resolve, the Run is not degraded — it is absent, and the identity outcomes below apply instead.
capabilityDerivation.neverStored: effectiveCapability is computed on read. Writing it into the sealed Run is a contract violation (RC-2).

availabilityModel.ledger: append-only; never rewrites the sealed Run

unitStates.meaning: the unit resolves and passes integrity
temporarily unresolvable — removable media, unmounted store, transient IO. May recover.
deleted by an explicit policy purge action
deleted by explicit policy retention expiry
a required producer/environment object of a replay closure is not obtainable offline

availabilityModel.terminalMonotonicity: The set of terminally lost units is append-only. A terminal state never returns to AVAILABLE. OUTAGE may return to AVAILABLE, so effective capability may dip and recover under transient loss — but the CEILING implied by terminal losses is non-increasing.
availabilityModel.whyNotStrictMonotone: v4 explicitly requires that temporary outage stay distinguishable from expiry, purge, corruption, and missing dependencies. Collapsing recoverable outage into permanent loss would make an unmounted volume indistinguishable from a deletion and would encourage spurious re-analysis.
availabilityModel.reporting: A degradation report names each unavailable unit and its cause. A single Run-wide degradation word is a contract violation (RC-6, carrying v4 immutabilityAndRetention.reporting).

custodyPolicy.perObligation: Custody strategy — retain frozen evidence, or retain an exact deterministic regeneration closure — is selected per proof obligation, never promoted into a universal tier. This is inherited unchanged from v4 orthogonalDimensions.
custodyPolicy.resolvedBy: the host admission boundary, from the project storage and retention policy
custodyPolicy.producersMayNotSelect: A producer/extension may not choose its own custody strategy or declare its output adequate. Proof adequacy is host-owned (RA-3/E3).

defaultPosture.rule: No managed durable user-derived write occurs without an explicit project storage and retention policy.
defaultPosture.whenPolicyMissing: The request is either explicitly advisory/ephemeral, or rejected if durable or authoritative evidence was requested.
defaultPosture.signOff: CD-RT-5 accepted 2026-07-31 by product owner: zero implicit durable retention for greenfield. First-run UX documented separately and is not an architecture concern.
defaultPosture.nonInteractiveClients: Agents and CI use a pre-provisioned or versioned policy; they never answer an interactive consent question implicitly.

admissionTimePinning.rule: For every declared authoritative input, the host resolves effective capability ONCE at admission and pins the units that capability depends on for the duration of the Run.
admissionTimePinning.why: Without this, a purge landing between admission and use produces a Run that consumed evidence it can no longer justify — a time-of-check/time-of-use hole that would silently reintroduce RA-CE-2.
admissionTimePinning.interactionWithPins: This composes with RA-7/E7: a retained authoritative Run already pins its own evidence. This clause extends the same pin to evidence a NEW Run consumes as an authoritative input.
admissionTimePinning.oneShotFit: In the one-shot topology that is the sealed architecture floor (R-1), admission and use are separated by a single process lifetime, so the pin is a process-scoped lease rather than a distributed lock.

purgeSemantics.explicitAction: Purge is an explicit, recorded policy action with a stated scope and cause. Cache GC is not purge and may never remove a unit pinned by a retained authoritative Run (RA-7/E7, RA-CE-4).
purgeSemantics.neverRewritesHistory: Purge appends unit state transitions to the retention ledger. It never edits the sealed Run, its capability, or its evidence inventory.
purgeSemantics.neverSilentlyTrusts: A purged no-match becomes UNVERIFIABLE. It never degrades to trusted, assumed, or still-passing. That is RA-CE-2 and it is the single most important thing this artifact must not permit.
purgeSemantics.targetedPurgeIsSupported: Purging material derived from a specific path or subject affects exactly the units that contain it. Unrelated Runs are untouched; affected Runs demote to the capability their surviving units support.
purgeSemantics.deletionResidual: Real deletion behaviour for deduplicated and backup-held objects remains a storage-architecture question — see threat-model deletionProtocol. This artifact requires that purge be honest about what it does and does not promise; it does not claim forensic erasure.

outcomeMapping.principle: Every typed outcome in this model maps onto the ALREADY-CLOSED D9 vocabulary. This artifact introduces no reason code and no error code.
outcomeMapping.whyThatMatters: D9 codeVocabulary is closed:true and its codes are DERIVED from closed cause enums, not authored. A retention model that needed a new code would reopen a contract-complete surface with 44 goldens and a 13-mutation suite. It does not need one — the demoted-input case is structurally the request-rejected/unsatisfiable case D9 already carries.

map.ration: Inspection asserts no authority. The command answered the question asked. Per-unit availability is envelope content, distinct from HostTermination (invariant-verdict-vs-termination).

map.situation: authoritative use (gate, baseline mutation, waiver, compliance assertion) of a Run whose effective capability is below verifiable
map.precedent: d9 golden analysis-ephemeral-when-authoritative-required — caller declares an authoritative postcondition the resolved input cannot meet. Same remedy class: restate the request or produce a fresh authoritative Run. No new remedy behind the code.

map.situation: durable or authoritative evidence requested with no explicit retention policy

map.precedent: d9 golden query-addressed-run-expired; invariant-identity-expiry requires the tombstone.
d9 invariant-identity-expiry — absence of tombstone is exactly the distinction.

map.situation: evidence unit resolves but fails integrity
map.rationale: Integrity failure is a fault, not an authorised loss. It is repairable, not restated — a different remedy class from purge, which is why it must not share REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE.

map.situation: content-addressed object cannot be linked or materialised
map.rationale: Existing code with an existing remedy ('run store repair').

invariants.assert: The sealed assurance capability and the sealed evidence inventory are immutable. No availability event, purge, expiry, or corruption rewrites them.
Effective capability is DERIVED at read time from the sealed capability and live unit states. It is never persisted into the sealed Run.
Effective capability never exceeds sealed capability, and the set of terminally lost units is append-only — a terminal loss never returns to AVAILABLE.
A Run whose effective capability is below verifiable is never accepted as an authoritative input; the attempt terminates request-rejected/REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE.
Effective capability for every declared authoritative input is resolved at admission and its supporting units pinned for the Run's duration.
A degradation report identifies each unavailable unit and its cause. One Run-wide degradation word is insufficient.
Inspecting a degraded Run succeeds and reports honestly. Loss of proof restricts authority, never readability of history.
Purge is explicit, recorded, and never converts an unverifiable claim into a trusted or still-passing one.
No managed durable user-derived write occurs without an explicit storage and retention policy.
Every outcome in this model uses the existing closed D9 vocabulary. Introducing a new reason or error code here is a contract violation requiring a D9 revision.

counterexampleFixtures.why: Same discipline v4 imposed on evidence.v1 (A1-RTV4-01): the architecture is incomplete until each counterexample is executable and rejected BY ITS NAMED INVARIANT.

fixtures.scenario: a Run with a PURGED fact partition is accepted as an authoritative baseline
effective capability is written into the sealed Run manifest
a Run sealed as recorded is read as verifiable because its units happen to be present
a PURGED unit transitions back to AVAILABLE
degradation is reported as a single Run-wide word with no unit detail
inspecting a degraded Run is rejected instead of reported
a purged no-match is reported as still passing on trust
a durable authoritative write proceeds with no resolved retention policy
the model introduces a bespoke error code for evidence loss
effective capability is resolved after admission, so a mid-Run purge is not caught

acceptingFixtures.scenario: all units available; sealed verifiable; used as an authoritative gate
one purged unit; inspection succeeds with per-unit reasons
the same degraded Run refused for authoritative use with the existing code
an unmounted store returns; effective capability recovers because OUTAGE is not terminal
a replayable Run loses an environment object; it demotes to verifiable and remains a valid gate

responsibilityBoundaries.owns: the append-only unit availability ledger, policy expiry, purge execution, inventory, deletion reporting
responsibilityBoundaries.mustNot: rewrite a sealed Run, or allow cache GC to remove a pinned unit

responsibilityBoundaries.owns: resolving effective capability for declared authoritative inputs, pinning them, and refusing before any durable write
responsibilityBoundaries.mustNot: admit an authoritative use whose resolved input is below verifiable

responsibilityBoundaries.owns: presenting sealed capability and effective capability as distinct fields with per-unit causes
responsibilityBoundaries.mustNot: collapse them into one word, or present sealed capability alone as current assurance

resolves.V10: RESOLVED-BY-DISPOSITION. Item 1 and the item-2 closure are discharged by evidence.v1 (independently reviewed and adjudicated). Item 2's custody policy and item 3's purge/availability semantics are decided here. The measurement residual is retained and named below — it is not part of the contradiction.
resolves.CD-RT-3: CARRIED — sealedTier immutable plus availability projection is exactly sealedVersusEffective.
resolves.CD-RT-5: SIGNED OFF — zero implicit durable retention accepted by product 2026-07-31.
resolves.A1-RTV4-03: CLOSED by the CD-RT-5 sign-off; defaultPosture is now product-accepted rather than candidate posture.
resolves.B-RT-04: CLOSED — the immutable/mutable split is now a derivation function plus an append-only ledger, not a mutable field in a sealed manifest.
resolves.B-RT-07: CLOSED — nothing is retained by default; source witness retention requires explicit policy grant (inherited from v4 privacyBoundary and now gated by a signed-off default posture).

retainedResiduals.statement: Measure the no-match Merkle fold plus reverification cost INCLUDING retained fact custody on representative repositories.
retainedResiduals.blocks: cost-advantage claims only — no constant-size or orders-of-magnitude claim is authorized until measured
retainedResiduals.doesNotBlock: implementing the evidence obligations or this custody model

retainedResiduals.statement: Qualify storage exposure detector catalogs against real sync/backup clients on supported platforms.
Real deletion behaviour for deduplicated and backup-held objects.
retainedResiduals.note: Purge here promises an honest recorded transition and pin release, explicitly not forensic erasure.

retainedResiduals.statement: This artifact is authored, not yet independently reviewed. Seal requires a second author for the RC-CE fixtures, matching the independence rule v4 imposed on evidence.v1.
retainedResiduals.note: implementable:true is not DISCHARGED. This artifact is a candidate.

knownLimitations: Authored by the agent closing the phase, not independently reviewed. The RC-CE fixtures and the checker share one author — the exact condition A1-RTV4-01 called out for evidence.v1.

The unit-granularity choice assumes evidence units are individually addressable and individually purgeable. A storage layout that only supports whole-Run deletion would force the rejected Run-atomic model; that constraint belongs to the storage architecture and is not yet fixed.

Effective-capability derivation is specified as a pure function over unit states. It says nothing about how expensive it is to determine those states for a Run with many thousands of units; that is a measurement question adjacent to A1-RTV4-02.
The admission-time pin is specified for the one-shot topology that is the architecture floor. A resident host would need a real lease protocol, which is parked with R-1 residency.
Fact tuples remain user-derived and privacy-classed. Removing source custody does not make the retained evidence non-sensitive (inherited from evidence.v1).
confidence: high on the sealed/effective split, the D9 mapping reusing only closed vocabulary, and terminal monotonicity; medium-high on unit granularity, which depends on a storage layout not yet fixed; medium on cost, which is A1-RTV4-02 and deliberately unresolved.
sealRecommendation: SEAL-WITH-CHANGES once independently reviewed. The V10 architecture fork is closed: the proof construction was already selected and verified elsewhere, the custody policy and default posture are now decided and product-signed, and evidence loss maps onto typed outcomes without reopening D9. Remaining items are measurement, storage-architecture, and the process requirement for a second reviewer — none of them architecture forks.
